title: Clicky action
description: One thing Clicky says, shows or does. Shared by every backend (and by the Linux app later). Coordinates are pixels in the screenshot the model was sent: origin top-left, x right, y down.

say.description: Speak to the user. Plain conversational sentences; no markdown.

point.description: Fly the buddy to a spot on the screenshot and point at it, e.g. a button you are talking about. Use this instead of describing where something is.

label.description: Short caption shown by the pointer, e.g. "Share".

highlight.description: Draw a glowing box around an area of the screenshot, e.g. a panel or a group of controls.

draw.description: Draw on the screen to explain something. arrow: points are [from, to]. circle: points are [centre] and radius is required. underline: points are [start, end]. freehand: 2 to 64 points.

step.description: One step of a walkthrough the user wants to learn (at most 15 steps). Give one step at a time, then wait for the user. x and y mark where the user should act.

click.description: Click on the computer for the user. Only when the user asked you to do something for them.

target.description: Name of the control, e.g. "Save button", so it can be found without moving the mouse.

type.description: Type text into the focused field.

key.description: Press a key or shortcut, e.g. "Enter", "Ctrl+S", "Alt+Tab".

repeat.description: Press it this many times, e.g. 3 for Tab Tab Tab.

scroll.description: Scroll at a spot on the screenshot.

wait.description: Wait for the screen to settle, e.g. after opening an app.

ask_permission.description: Ask before acting on the computer, and always before anything that sends, deletes, buys, publishes or cannot be undone. Then stop and wait for the answer.

action.description: What you are about to do, e.g. "Send the email to Priya".

done.description: The task you were doing on the computer is finished (or cannot be finished).

open_url.description: Open a web page in Clicky's own browser window (a separate Chrome profile the user can sign in to). Use it instead of clicking through a browser to reach a page. Only http and https addresses.

use_tool.description: Call one of the user's connected app tools, listed in the conversation with their input schemas. Clicky asks the user first when a tool can change anything, and sends you back its result.

input.description: The tool's arguments, matching its input schema.

routine.description: Set up a routine: a prompt Clicky runs by itself on a schedule while it is open, e.g. "brief me every morning" or "check my inbox every few hours". Use it only when the user asks for something to happen regularly or at a later time. Clicky shows it to the user, who saves it or not, so say in a sentence what you are setting up and never say it is saved.

prompt.description: What to do each time, as a complete instruction that makes sense on its own later, without the screen or this conversation.

schedule.description: When it runs, in the user's local time. 'every morning' = daily 08:00, 'every evening' = daily 18:00, 'every weekday' = weekdays, 'every few hours' = every 180 minutes from 09:00 until 21:00, 'every hour' = every 60 minutes.

days.description: weekly, or to limit daily or every to some days.

from.description: every: HH:mm of the first run each day.

until.description: every: no runs at or after this HH:mm.

cron.description: cron: five fields (minute hour day-of-month month day-of-week). Only when nothing else fits.
